name: Primary Eosinophilic Gastrointestinal Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Primary Eosinophilic Gastrointestinal Disease

criteria.description: Presence of marked eosinophilic infiltration in gastrointestinal tissue biopsy exceeding normal thresholds
Exclusion of secondary causes of gastrointestinal eosinophilia such as parasitic infection, drug reactions, or systemic diseases
Presence of gastrointestinal symptoms consistent with eosinophilic infiltration such as abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
Peripheral blood eosinophilia supporting diagnosis but not mandatory

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histologic evidence of eosinophilic infiltration in GI tissue with exclusion of secondary causes and presence of compatible clinical symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires comprehensive clinical, histological, and laboratory evaluation to exclude other causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked eosinophilic infiltration of gastrointestinal mucosa
searchTerms: high eosinophil count in gut lining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic abdominal pain localized to affected GI segment
searchTerms: chronic stomach pain in specific area
weight loss from poor nutrient absorption
swelling in limbs from low blood protein

rare.symptomName: Gastrointestinal obstruction due to muscular layer involvement
searchTerms: gut obstruction caused by muscle layer
bowel blockage due to muscle involvement
hole or tear in digestive tract

imaging: Endoscopic mucosal edema, erythema, and ulcerations
Barium studies showing segmental bowel wall thickening
Ultrasound or CT demonstrating bowel wall thickening and ascites
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible association with atopic predisposition
other: Histopathology showing eosinophilic infiltration without evidence of secondary causes

distinguishingFeatures: Identification of parasitic organisms in stool or tissue
Eosinophilia secondary to infection rather than primary GI infiltration
Multi-organ eosinophilic infiltration beyond GI tract
Presence of cardiac, pulmonary, or neurological involvement
Histologic features of chronic inflammation with crypt architectural distortion
Presence of granulomas in Crohn’s disease

redFlags: Signs of bowel obstruction or perforation
Rapidly progressive weight loss and malnutrition
references: Liacouras CA, et al. Eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders: updated consensus recommendations for children and adults. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2011.
Molina-Infante J, et al. Eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases: clinical and pathophysiological insights. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2020.
